found_while: 2026-11-10: link batches 1-2 and the precision review

items.name: Birth of Akbar
items.why: Death of Akbar exists but not his birth; his life could become a span.

items.name: Akbar Becomes Mughal Emperor
items.why: Akbar's accession is missing; it would follow Humayun Recaptures Delhi and begin his reign.

items.name: Reign of Akbar
items.why: Would hold the Mansabdari system, Haldighati and Din-i-Ilahi as part_of, instead of linking them only to the whole empire.

items.name: Shah Jahan Becomes Mughal Emperor
items.why: The Mughal succession chain skips Shah Jahan (Death of Jahangir → Aurangzeb); the Taj Mahal is his.

items.name: Reign of Shah Jahan
items.why: The Taj Mahal's patron has no span or event of his own.

items.name: Death of Aurangzeb
items.why: The usual marker of the start of Mughal decline; 'Mughal Empire Reaches Maximum Extent' (1707) stands in for it now.

items.name: Battle of Khanwa
items.why: Babur's victory over Rana Sanga, which secured Mughal rule after Panipat.

items.name: Battle of Chausa
items.why: Sher Shah Suri's first defeat of Humayun, a year before Kanauj.

items.name: Sur Empire
items.why: Sher Shah Suri's empire between Humayun's exile and return; the Mughal story has a gap here.

items.name: Iltutmish Becomes Sultan of Delhi
items.why: The Delhi sultans chain jumps from Aibak to Razia; Iltutmish was between them.

items.name: Mamluk Dynasty of Delhi
items.why: The Delhi Sultanate's five dynasties have no spans, so the sultans can't be grouped by dynasty.

items.name: Khalji Dynasty
items.why: Second Delhi Sultanate dynasty.

items.name: Tughlaq Dynasty
items.why: Third Delhi Sultanate dynasty.

items.name: Sayyid Dynasty
items.why: Fourth Delhi Sultanate dynasty; nothing covers 1414-1451 in South Asia.

items.name: Lodi Dynasty
items.why: Last Delhi Sultanate dynasty, ended at Panipat.

items.name: Company Rule in India
items.why: The East India Company's rule between Plassey and the British Raj has no span.

items.name: Government of India Act 1858
items.why: Transferred rule from the Company to the Crown: the start of the British Raj (would 'begin' it).

items.name: Indian Independence Movement
items.why: The whole movement (from the Congress's founding, or 1857). The current span covers only its Gandhian era (1920-1947).

items.name: Gandhi Returns to India
items.why: Gandhi's return from South Africa opened his role in the movement.

items.name: Anglo-Mysore Wars
items.why: Four wars; only the second has an event, and nothing groups them.

items.name: Founding of the Khalsa
items.why: Guru Gobind Singh's founding of the Khalsa, a defining moment of Sikhism.

items.name: Sikh Empire
items.why: Ranjit Singh's empire in the Punjab has no span.

items.name: Kalinga War
items.why: The war that led to Ashoka's conversion; it would 'contribute to' Ashoka Converts to Buddhism. (Ashoka Converts to Buddhism mentions it.)

items.name: Reign of Ashoka
items.why: Ashoka's accession and conversion exist as events, but not his reign.

items.name: Battle of Sekigahara
items.why: The victory that gave Tokugawa Ieyasu power; it would precede the Tokugawa Shogunate.

items.name: Tokugawa Ieyasu Becomes Shogun
items.why: Would 'begin' the Tokugawa Shogunate (the Meiji Restoration already ends it).

items.name: Commodore Perry Arrives in Japan
items.why: Opened Japan to the West, leading to the Meiji Restoration.

items.name: Qing Capture of Beijing
items.why: Would 'end' the Ming Dynasty and 'begin' the Qing.

items.name: Treaty of Nanking
items.why: Ended the First Opium War and ceded Hong Kong; links to the 1997 handover. (The First Opium War event lists it as an alias.)

items.name: Fall of the Ming Dynasty
items.why: Li Zicheng's capture of Beijing and the last Ming emperor's suicide.

items.name: First Punic War
items.why: The Punic Wars have no sub-spans: Zama can't be linked to the war it ended.

items.name: Second Punic War
items.why: Hannibal's war; Zama 'ended' it (it can't end the Punic Wars as a whole).

items.name: Third Punic War
items.why: The war that destroyed Carthage.

items.name: Destruction of Carthage
items.why: Would 'end' the Punic Wars.

items.name: War of the Third Coalition
items.why: Trafalgar's own war, between the Napoleonic Wars and the battle.

items.name: Napoleon Crowned Emperor
items.why: A central Napoleonic moment, missing.

items.name: Coup of 18 Brumaire
items.why: Napoleon's seizure of power: would 'end' the French Revolution, which has no ender now.

items.name: Execution of Louis XVI
items.why: A defining event of the French Revolution.

items.name: Reign of Terror
items.why: The Revolution's most violent phase has no span.

items.name: Division of the Roman Empire
items.why: The split into East and West at Theodosius's death: would 'begin' the Fall of the Western Roman Empire.

items.name: Visigoths Sack Rome
items.why: The first sack of Rome in 800 years, part of the Western Empire's fall.

items.name: Battle of the Somme
items.why: One of the First World War's defining battles.

items.name: United States Enters World War I
items.why: Turned the First World War; missing from the WWI sequence.

items.name: Battle of Stalingrad
items.why: The Eastern Front's turning point; the WWII sequence jumps from Pearl Harbor to D-Day.

items.name: Battle of Midway
items.why: The Pacific War's turning point.

items.name: Germany Surrenders (V-E Day)
items.why: The end of the war in Europe; the WWII sequence goes from D-Day to Hiroshima without it. ("World War Two Ends" covers both surrenders in one event.)

items.name: Cold War
items.why: A major span with no bar: Cold War Begins and the Berlin Wall's fall exist only as events.

items.name: Apollo-Soyuz Test Project
items.why: The joint US-Soviet flight some historians take as the Space Race's end.

items.name: Korean Armistice Agreement
items.why: Would 'end' the Korean War.

items.name: Fall of Saigon
items.why: Would 'end' the Vietnam War, which has no ender.

items.name: Battles of Lexington and Concord
items.why: Would 'begin' the American Revolution.

items.name: Battle of Fort Sumter
items.why: Would 'begin' the American Civil War.

items.name: Fall of Tenochtitlan
items.why: The more exact end of the Aztec Empire than the 1519 start of the conquest (which 'ends' it now).

items.name: Mansa Musa's Pilgrimage to Mecca
items.why: Africa before 1500 is thin; the Mali Empire's most famous moment is missing.

items.name: Kingdom of Aksum
items.why: A major African state with no span (Africa before 1500 is thin).

items.name: Great Zimbabwe
items.why: Southern Africa's great medieval city has no span.

items.name: Songhai Empire
items.why: West Africa's largest empire after Mali has no span.

items.name: Olmec Civilization
items.why: Mesoamerica before the Maya is empty.

items.name: Unification of Egypt
items.why: Narmer's unification, the start of Pharaonic Egypt; nothing marks it.
